newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar stuck in narrow range in quiet Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar stuck in narrow range in quiet Tokyo.

text.p: 0523 GMT --*Dollar moving narrowly in afternoon Tokyo, with trade quiet amid no fresh market-moving factors and ahead of U.S. April international trade data due later in day.
*Dollar sandwiched between bids from U.S. traders and Japanese investors, including life insurers, near 113.20 yen and offers from exporters near 113.70 yen.
*A trust bank dealer said some short-covering by interbank dealers detected as dollar's downside remains solid.
*Possible stop-loss buying may emerge near 113.80/85 yen if dollar absorbs heavy offers near 113.70 yen, a dealer said.
*"Japanese investors, public fund bodies and pension funds may be raising their bids level to 113.20 yen," the second dealer said.
0300 GMT-- Dollar was off its earlier lows against yen by Tokyo midday but remained caught in a tight range.
*Dollar had eased against yen earlier in the day following remarks by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.
*Rubin said on Wednesday in Washington that it was "very important" that Japan achieve domestic demand-led growth and avoid a sustained increase in its trade surplus.
